Insert data into several tables in one transaction

Source: R/util_database_load_many.R
insert_data_many.Rd

Inserts one data.table into each table of a list. On PostgreSQL, one psql session loads every table in one transaction, so by default the call stores every row or no row. The one exception is a duplicate key with confirm_insert_via_nrow = TRUE: csdb then inserts table by table.

Usage

insert_data_many(
  tables,
  newdata,
  confirm_insert_via_nrow = FALSE,
  verbose = TRUE,
  load_timeout = 3600
)

Arguments

tables

A list of DBTable_v9 objects.

newdata

A list of data.tables, one for each table, in the order of tables.

confirm_insert_via_nrow

See DBTable_v9$insert_data().

verbose

See DBTable_v9$insert_data().

load_timeout

The longest time in seconds that the psql session MAY run. csdb then stops it with an error of class csdb_load_ambiguous.

Value

NULL, invisibly.

Details

On PostgreSQL, csdb starts psql once, with --single-transaction, and runs one \copy for each table. A table whose data.table is NULL or has no rows gets no \copy. After each \copy, the script compares the stored rows with the rows sent. A difference raises an error before the commit, so the server stores no row in any table.

The transaction holds a lock on every table until it commits, so a TRUNCATE or an index change on one of them waits. The session waits at most 60 s for one lock. After a longer wait, a deadlock or a refused login, csdb runs the whole session again, at most 3 attempts in total. A connection that breaks after the load starts is not run again, and the error says to count the rows first. So is a row count that differs after psql exits.

A duplicate key stops the session. With confirm_insert_via_nrow = TRUE, csdb then calls $insert_data(confirm_insert_via_nrow = TRUE) on each table, which upserts a table that stops on the duplicate key.

With another driver, or with tables that have different connection settings, csdb calls $insert_data() on each table in turn.

Examples

# \donttest{
# SQLite has no psql, so csdb inserts into each table in turn here.
db_config <- list(driver = "SQLite", db = tempfile(fileext = ".sqlite"))
connection <- DBConnection_v9$new(driver = "SQLite", db = db_config$db)
tables <- lapply(c("cases_a", "cases_b"), function(name) {
  DBTable_v9$new(
    dbconfig = db_config,
    table_name = name,
    field_types = c("id" = "INTEGER", "n" = "INTEGER"),
    keys = "id",
    dbconnection = connection
  )
})
insert_data_many(
  tables,
  list(
    data.table::data.table(id = 1:2, n = c(5L, 7L)),
    data.table::data.table(id = 1L, n = 3L)
  )
)
#> Creating table cases_a
#> Creating table cases_b
tables[[1]]$nrow()
#> [1] 2
connection$disconnect()
# }
